title: easyssf 0.4.0: a column renamed
body:
easyssf 0.4.0 is on Maven Central, org.easyssf:easyssf-receiver-spring-boot-starter:0.4.0 and the other modules alongside. It is a small release with one schema change: the column PROCESSED_AT of EASYSSF_PROCESSED_SET is now STATE_CHANGED_AT, which is what it has held since 0.3.0, the time of the claim as well as that of the completion, and it fences the claim.

Upgrading: existing tables need ALTER TABLE EASYSSF_PROCESSED_SET RENAME COLUMN PROCESSED_AT TO STATE_CHANGED_AT, the migration script V0_4_0__state_changed_at.sql, which works on H2, PostgreSQL and MySQL 8. Where the receiver may create tables it renames the column on startup; otherwise it names the statement in the error. The release notes have the details.

title: easyssf 0.3.0: durable poll delivery, several instances, typed CAEP and RISC events
body:
easyssf 0.3.0 is on Maven Central, org.easyssf:easyssf-receiver-spring-boot-starter:0.3.0 and the other modules alongside. The release makes poll delivery survive restarts and run on several instances, and gives handlers typed access to CAEP and RISC events.

  • Poll acknowledgements wait in an SsfPollAckStore, in memory or durably in the database with JdbcSsfPollAckStore, until a poll request has carried them, so a SET handled right before a restart is acknowledged afterwards instead of being delivered again. Stopping the poller sends the pending acknowledgements with a last request; the health details and a gauge count them.
  • Long polling (RFC 8936, section 2.5): the poller keeps one request outstanding that the transmitter holds until SETs are available, easyssf.receiver.poll.long-polling in the Spring Boot starter, off by default.
  • A SET is claimed in the de-duplication store while its handlers run: another instance that receives it meanwhile neither handles nor acknowledges it, and a claim older than the lease counts as abandoned, so two instances sharing the JDBC stores never acknowledge a SET one of them failed on.
  • SsfCaepEventHandler and SsfRiscEventHandler dispatch the events of a SET to a method per event type, onSessionRevoked, onAssuranceLevelChange, onAccountDisabled and the others, with SsfCaepEvent and SsfRiscEvent for the claims the specifications define. An event type easyssf does not know yet reaches onOtherCaepEvent or onOtherRiscEvent.
  • The documentation now says that processing is at least once; idempotencyKey() on the SET and the event context, the issuer and jti, is the key for a handler's side effects.
  • easyssf-receiver-jdbc ships versioned migration scripts, and where the receiver may create tables it adds the new column and table on startup; otherwise it names the statements to run. The JDBC stores are now tested on MySQL as well as on H2 and PostgreSQL.

Upgrading: the table EASYSSF_PROCESSED_SET gained the column STATE and the schema a third table, EASYSSF_POLL_ACK; SsfJtiDedupStore has claim, processed and forget, and seenBefore is deprecated. The release notes list all changes. The Quarkus extension quarkus-openid-ssf 0.3.0 stays on easyssf 0.2.0.

title: A tools page: generate and inspect Security Event Tokens
body:
easyssf.org has a tools page. Its Security Event Token generator builds a SET for any event type of SSF 1.0, CAEP 1.0, RISC 1.0 and SCIM Events (RFC 9967): pick the event and you get a complete example, then change the subject, the claims and the token. The subject can be any RFC 9493 identifier, the scim identifier or a complex subject with its members; every claim a specification defines has its field, and custom claims can be merged into the event and into the SET, to try what a specification does not define yet. The SET is shown as JSON and signed as a JWT with an RS256 or ES256 key generated in your browser.

  • Copy event copies the payload alone, for a transmitter such as Keycloak that wraps it in a SET itself; Copy as link gives a link that opens the generator with the same SET.
  • Named token presets keep the issuer, audience and signature of a demo setup in the browser's storage.
  • The inspector decodes a SET you received and names its event types.
  • The event types list every event with its URI, claims, the section of its specification and the alias easyssf accepts for it.

Everything runs in the browser; nothing you enter is sent to a server. The page is static HTML and JavaScript in the website repository.

title: quarkus-openid-ssf 0.3.0 brings SCIM Events to Quarkus
body:
The Quarkiverse extension quarkus-openid-ssf 0.3.0 is on Maven Central as io.quarkiverse.openid-ssf:quarkus-openid-ssf-receiver:0.3.0, built on easyssf 0.2.0. A SET that reports a change of a SCIM resource (RFC 9967) is verified like any other, the event types have their aliases, ScimProvDeactivate say, and SsfScimEventHandler hands the events to a method per operation. Nothing has to be configured, and nothing changes for existing applications.

A new example, example-scim-provisioning, mirrors SCIM users into a local directory, driven by a demo SCIM service provider over the test transmitter of easyssf, because Keycloak does not emit SCIM Events. The getting started guide uses 0.3.0; the release notes have the details.

title: easyssf 0.2.0: SCIM Events
body:
easyssf 0.2.0 is on Maven Central, org.easyssf:easyssf-receiver-spring-boot-starter:0.2.0 and the other modules alongside. The release adds SCIM Events, RFC 9967, to the receiver: a SCIM service provider reports the provisioning changes of its users and groups as Security Event Tokens, and an application mirrors them without polling the SCIM API.

  • The twelve event types under urn:ietf:params:scim:event: with aliases such as ScimProvCreateFull and ScimProvDeactivate, and the scim subject identifier with SsfScimSubject for the resource it names.
  • SsfScimEvent, the typed payload: the resource as data of a full event, the attributes of a notice event, the ETag version and the asynchronous response.
  • SsfScimEventHandler, which dispatches the SCIM Events of a SET to a method per operation: create, patch, put, delete, activate, deactivate.
  • The OIDC client integration matches a scim resource with the logged-in user by configurable pairs of SCIM attribute and claim, by default externalId and id against sub and userName against preferred_username, so a deactivation or deletion ends the user's sessions.
  • A new example, example-scim-provisioning, mirrors SCIM users into a local directory, driven by the test transmitter because Keycloak does not emit SCIM Events.
  • The README now shows plain Java, Spring Boot and Quarkus side by side, the Spring Boot starter has a README of its own, and pull requests build on CI.

The tools page generates SCIM Events, and every other SSF, CAEP and RISC event, as signed SETs to try a receiver with. The release notes list all changes.

title: Quarkus support: quarkus-openid-ssf 0.2.0 is built on easyssf
body:
The Quarkiverse extension quarkus-openid-ssf 0.2.0 is on Maven Central as io.quarkiverse.openid-ssf:quarkus-openid-ssf-receiver:0.2.0. Its protocol code is replaced by easyssf 0.1.0: SET verification, metadata discovery, stream management, push and poll delivery, de-duplication and the OAuth2 client credentials. The extension keeps what is Quarkus, the configuration, the CDI wiring, the Vert.x push route, the poll scheduler, the token providers, Micrometer, the Dev UI and native image support. The getting started guide has a Quarkus tab.

New with the release:

  • Built and tested against Quarkus 3.27 LTS.
  • Several transmitters per application, a JDBC de-duplication store over the default datasource and a SmallRye Health check, the same features the Spring Boot starter has.
  • The strict SET validation of easyssf: the top-level sub_id of SSF 1.0 with a legacy mode for older transmitters, critical subject members, HTTPS for the transmitter.
  • The four receiver plans of the OpenID conformance suite run against the extension, and two new examples, a resource server and a web application with Keycloak, mirror the Spring Boot examples.

0.2.0 changes the event handler SPI, the push and poll semantics and the metric names of the extension; the release notes walk through the migration from 0.1.x.

title: easyssf 0.1.0, the first release
body:
easyssf 0.1.0 is on Maven Central: org.easyssf:easyssf-receiver-spring-boot-starter:0.1.0 for Spring Boot 4.1 applications, easyssf-receiver for everything else, easyssf-receiver-jdbc for the database-backed stores and easyssf-test for the tests of your own receiver.

What the release contains:

  • A receiver for the OpenID Shared Signals Framework 1.0 with push and poll delivery, stream management and verification, de-duplication and the CAEP session and token revocation handlers; it passes the four receiver plans of the OpenID conformance suite (SSF 1.0 and the CAEP Interop Profile, push and poll).
  • Strict by default: SETs need the top-level sub_id of SSF 1.0 (a legacy mode accepts older transmitters), critical subject members a receiver does not understand are rejected, transmitters must use HTTPS, and only asymmetric signature algorithms are accepted.
  • Several transmitters per application, issuer-scoped revocations, a health indicator and Micrometer metrics for Spring Boot.
  • The framework-free modules are Java modules; every artifact is signed, ships a CycloneDX SBOM and a self-contained POM.

The release notes list the changes; SECURITY.md has the signing key.

title: Several transmitters per application
body:
A receiver can now take events from more than one transmitter, several Keycloak realms for instance. The settings at easyssf.receiver.* keep configuring the one transmitter most applications have; further ones go under easyssf.receiver.transmitters.<name>.*, each complete on its own.

  • The issuer of a SET selects the transmitter that verifies it, so one push endpoint serves all of them, each authenticating with its own header. Polled transmitters are polled independently.
  • The beans of the single-transmitter setup are unchanged; the new SsfTransmitters bean holds every transmitter by name and issuer, and SsfTransmitterCustomizer beans adjust them before they are built.
  • Metrics carry a transmitter tag, and the health indicator lists every transmitter.
  • For receivers without Spring Boot: SsfTransmitter, SsfTransmitters and the issuer-routing verifier are in easyssf-receiver.

title: Full subject identifiers, a health indicator and test support
body:
A round of changes after a review of the API, before the first release.

  • Subjects as RFC 9493 defines them. SsfSubjectIdentifier represents every format, and SsfSubject exposes all members of a complex subject. The shortcuts for user, session and email are unchanged. Matching an iss_sub identifier now requires the issuer as well as the subject, and token revocations are scoped to the issuer of the token.
  • HTTPS for the transmitter. The issuer and every endpoint in its metadata must use HTTPS; loopback addresses may use HTTP for local development, and easyssf.receiver.allow-insecure-http lifts the rule for test setups, with a warning at startup.
  • Your own event type aliases, registered in configuration or with SsfEventTypes.registerAlias, without redefining the built-in ones.
  • Typed transmitter metadata: specVersion(), deliveryMethodsSupported(), criticalSubjectMembers(), authorizationSchemes() and defaultSubjects().
  • Immutable value objects. Tokens, subjects, stream configurations and metadata copy what they are given and cannot be changed afterwards.
  • Health indicator easyssf for Spring Boot Actuator: whether the transmitter was reached, the stream is registered and the last poll succeeded, without calling the transmitter.
  • easyssf-test: the transmitter the easyssf tests use, as a module for the tests of your own receiver.
  • Every artifact ships with a CycloneDX SBOM, a self-contained POM and an automatic module name.

The schema of the EASYSSF_REVOCATION table gained an ISSUER column; nothing was released yet, so there is no migration.

title: Welcome to easyssf.org
body:
easyssf has a home. The project is a Java library and a Spring Boot 4.1 starter that turn an application into a receiver for the OpenID Shared Signals Framework: it verifies Security Event Tokens, rejects the access tokens and ends the sessions a CAEP event revokes, and hands every event to your own handlers.

Where things stand:

  • The receiver library has no framework dependencies; the Spring Boot starter covers the servlet stack, resource servers and OIDC clients.
  • Tested against the SSF transmitter of Keycloak 26.8 and the receiver test plans of the OpenID conformance suite.
  • The code is experimental and not yet published to Maven Central. Build it from source with ./mvnw install.

The source is on GitHub.
